article_title: Abnormal brain activation during speech perception and production in children and adults with reading difficulty
citation: Yang Fu, Xiaohui Yan, Jiaqi Mao, Haibin Su & Fan Cao. (2024). Abnormal brain activation during speech perception and production in children and adults with reading difficulty. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00266-2
title: fNIRS foreign speech perception and production paradigm for detecting RD
description: A paired-task neuroimaging protocol combining a passive rapid event-related Spanish CV-syllable perception task (120 pairs varying in syllable consistency and similarity to Chinese, four runs of around 4 min) with a speech production imitation task (26 multi-syllabic Chinese pseudowords and 26 Spanish words, 156 trials), recorded with a 48-channel continuous-wave fNIRS system. The article uses it because "fNIRS is especially suitable for studying speech production, because of its relative tolerance with motion artifacts." Activation patterns from these tasks feed an SVM classifier that distinguishes RD from controls.
requirements: Participants must be native Chinese speakers who have not learned Spanish, so foreign-speech similarity to the native language can be controlled
constraints: The article notes the relatively small sample size and cross-sectional design might have limited the capability of revealing developmental changes
target_learners: Chinese children (fifth grade) and young adults with and without reading difficulty
target_learning_goals: Foreign (Spanish) speech perception and production as behavioral and neural indices of phonological processing in reading difficulty
examples: Participants listened to 120 pairs of Spanish consonant-vowel syllables and imitated 26 Chinese pseudowords and 26 Spanish words while HbO responses were recorded with a NIRSport2 system at 4.4 Hz
key_sources: Yang Fu, Xiaohui Yan, Jiaqi Mao, Haibin Su & Fan Cao. (2024). Abnormal brain activation during speech perception and production in children and adults with reading difficulty. npj Science of Learning. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41539-024-00266-2

article_title: Development of Knowledge, Awareness, Global Warming Decreasing Behavior and Critical Thinking of Grade 11 Students Using the Four Noble Truths Method with Meta-Cognitive Techniques
citation: Sakkarin Chattuchai, Adisak Singseewo and Paitool Suksringarm. (2015). Development of knowledge, awareness, global warming decreasing behavior and critical thinking of grade 11 students using the Four Noble Truths method with meta-cognitive techniques. Educational Research and Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5897/ERR2015.2360
title: Five lesson plans on global warming using the FNT method with three metacognitive techniques
description: The study's instructional element is a set of five lesson plans on global warming, each consisting of three hours of learning per week, used over three weeks. The experimental plans use the FNT method with the three metacognitive techniques (intelligibility, plausibility, wide-applicability), while control plans use the traditional teaching method. Metacognitive questions were added to each stage of the FNT method in developing the plans.
requirements: Taught by the researcher over three weeks, three hours each, with instruments administered as pretest, immediate posttest and a four-week delayed posttest for behavior
examples: The two groups were taught by the researcher who used the 5 assigned lesson plans for three weeks, 3 h each
key_sources: Sakkarin Chattuchai, Adisak Singseewo and Paitool Suksringarm. (2015). Development of knowledge, awareness, global warming decreasing behavior and critical thinking of grade 11 students using the Four Noble Truths method with meta-cognitive techniques. Educational Research and Reviews. https://doi.org/10.5897/ERR2015.2360

article_title: Neurophysiological Insights into Multimedia-based Education: A PRISMA-ScR Review of fNIRS in Game-Integrated Learning Systems
citation: Sharmin, Shayla; Lucero-Palacios, Gael; Kiafar, Behdokht; Abrar, Md Fahim; Al-Ratrout, Mohammad; Raikwar, Aditya; Barmaki, Roghayeh Leila. (2024). Neurophysiological Insights into Multimedia-based Education: A PRISMA-ScR Review of fNIRS in Game-Integrated Learning Systems. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.02650v5
title: fNIRS as a portable cortical hemodynamic measurement tool for interactive learning environments
description: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) is the neurophysiological measurement tool examined across the reviewed studies. The review describes it as "a portable, non-invasive brain-imaging tool that measures changes in blood oxygenation in the cortex as an indirect measure of brain activity," suitable for interactive learning environments where fMRI faces practical constraints because it permits greater mobility and is less sensitive to electrical noise from screens and game devices. Eight commercial fNIRS system categories appeared in the corpus, with the Biopac fNIRS Imager most frequent (eight studies).
requirements: Interpretation alongside task context and complementary behavioral, learning, or subjective measures
constraints: fNIRS does not directly measure learning, engagement, mental effort, or cognitive load; it measures task-related cortical hemodynamic responses
target_learners: participants in game-integrated learning studies across age groups, including children, adults, and older adults
target_learning_goals: measuring task-related cortical hemodynamic responses during gameplay-based learning and skill acquisition
examples: Eight commercial system categories used across the corpus, including fNIRS Imager 1200/2000S (Biopac), NIRSport2 (NIRx), ETG-4000 (Hitachi), and Brite23 (Artinis)
key_sources: Sharmin, Shayla; Lucero-Palacios, Gael; Kiafar, Behdokht; Abrar, Md Fahim; Al-Ratrout, Mohammad; Raikwar, Aditya; Barmaki, Roghayeh Leila. (2024). Neurophysiological Insights into Multimedia-based Education: A PRISMA-ScR Review of fNIRS in Game-Integrated Learning Systems. arXiv. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.02650

article_title: Hybrid Deep Learning Model to Estimate Cognitive Effort from fNIRS Signals
citation: Shayla Sharmin and Roghayeh Leila Barmaki. 2025. Hybrid Deep Learning Model to Estimate Cognitive Effort from fNIRS Signals. Companion Proceedings of the 27th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction (ICMI Companion '25). https://doi.org/10.1145/3747327.3764901
title: fNIRS educational quiz dataset of 256 responses from 16 participants in a Unity-based graph theory game
description: A novel dataset collected during a Unity-based educational quiz game assessing graph theory concepts such as nodes, edges, and loops. It contains "total 256 responses in the dataset (16 × 16)" from 16 participants answering 16 questions, with fNIRS recorded at 10 Hz from 16 prefrontal optodes. The dataset is imbalanced, with 168 correct and 88 incorrect responses, and captures both hemodynamic responses and performance scores for continuous performance prediction.
requirements: fNIRS headband recording (18-channel fNIRS 2000S device) synchronized with the quiz interface via COBI Studio software
constraints: The dataset is imbalanced because participants generally performed well, which the authors say suggests task difficulty may need future adjustment
target_learners: adult learners in educational game settings
target_learning_goals: predicting task performance and cognitive effort from brain signals during learning
examples: Each question lasted 30 seconds; only the first 200 rows per question were retained, giving 16 participants x 16 questions x 200 time points x 16 optodes data points
key_sources: Shayla Sharmin and Roghayeh Leila Barmaki. 2025. Hybrid Deep Learning Model to Estimate Cognitive Effort from fNIRS Signals. Companion Proceedings of the 27th International Conference on Multimodal Interaction (ICMI Companion '25). https://doi.org/10.1145/3747327.3764901
